meta.title: Better-for-You Indulgence
meta.subtitle: A US + Australia market map of guilt-free food & beverage — by Arjun Kulshrestha
meta.author: Arjun Kulshrestha

galaxies.name: Protein as Pleasure
galaxies.tagline: Dessert-coded protein. Candy bars that happen to have macros.
galaxies.need_state: I want a treat that earns its place in my day.
galaxies.why_care: Protein has replaced 'low fat' as the universal health heuristic. The winning brands code as candy, cereal and popcorn — not gym supplements — which unlocks mass grocery and convenience channels.
galaxies.risks: Formulation arms race; novel-ingredient scrutiny (e.g. EPG); celebrity-brand noise; incumbents (Quest, Barebells) own shelf space.

galaxies.name: Sweet, Without the Sugar
galaxies.tagline: Candy, chocolate and dessert with the regret removed.
galaxies.need_state: I refuse to give up sweets — take out the sugar, not the joy.
galaxies.why_care: Sugar is the single most avoided ingredient in both the US and Australia. The unlock was taste parity plus fun branding — these brands sell in the candy aisle and at the chemist, not the diet aisle.
galaxies.risks: Sweetener fatigue (sugar alcohols, stevia aftertaste); private label moves fast; single-hero-SKU concentration.

galaxies.name: Functional Refreshment
galaxies.tagline: Soda rebuilt: prebiotics, no sugar, real flavour.
galaxies.need_state: I want the ritual of a Coke without drinking a Coke.
galaxies.why_care: The category that proved BFY indulgence is venture-scale: Poppi exited to PepsiCo for $1.95B and OLIPOP was last valued at $1.85B. Australia is running the same playbook 2–3 years behind the US.
galaxies.risks: US shelf is saturated post-Poppi; flavour/format copycats; big-soda response (Coke Simply Pop); prebiotic claims litigation.

galaxies.name: Gut Health & Free-From
galaxies.tagline: Indulgence engineered for sensitive stomachs and allergies.
galaxies.need_state: I want to eat like everyone else without paying for it later.
galaxies.why_care: Gut health is the fastest-growing wellness claim, and GLP-1 users need fibre and digestive support. Free-from brands win fierce loyalty because the alternative for these consumers is exclusion, not another brand.
galaxies.risks: Niche-to-mass leap is hard; medical-adjacent claims invite regulator attention; low-FODMAP is a small beachhead.

galaxies.name: Clean-Label Comfort
galaxies.tagline: Mac & cheese, ramen, tacos and snacks — with the label cleaned up.
galaxies.need_state: I want childhood comfort food I don't have to hide in my pantry.
galaxies.why_care: Nostalgia is the cheapest customer acquisition there is. Upgrading an existing habit (ramen, mac & cheese, popcorn) beats inventing a new one — and acquirers agree: Siete went for $1.2B, LesserEvil for ~$750M.
galaxies.risks: Premium price vs. $1 incumbent comparison; velocity pressure in mainstream grocery; 'clean label' is unregulated language.

galaxies.name: Culture-Led & Kids' Treats
galaxies.need_state: I buy the story (or my kids' lunchbox rules decide for me).
galaxies.why_care: Distribution is the moat — creators bring their own. Feastables hit $250M revenue in under three years off MrBeast's audience. Meanwhile parents are an underserved, rule-driven buyer (school policies, sugar limits) with high repeat purchase.
galaxies.risks: Key-person risk on creator brands; kids' marketing regulation; novelty purchase vs. true repeat.

companies.name: David
companies.product: 28g-protein, 0g-sugar, 150-calorie bars (and expanding formats)
companies.positioning: The most efficient protein per calorie, branded like a luxury object, not a supplement
companies.target: Protein-first consumers and GLP-1 users who treat macros as a daily budget
companies.differentiation: Vertical ingredient control — used its Series A to buy Epogee, sole supplier of the EPG fat replacer behind its calorie math
companies.channels: DTC-first, now 3,000+ US retail doors
companies.vc_take: Category-defining velocity: ~$100M revenue in year one and a supply-chain moat most CPG brands never build. The founder set (Peter Rahal, ex-RXBAR) is the operator archetype this thesis bets on.
companies.signal: $75M Series A (May 2025) led by Greenoaks with Valor; $725M valuation; ~$100M first-year revenue — verified

companies.name: Chomps
companies.product: Grass-fed beef, venison and turkey meat sticks
companies.positioning: Clean-ingredient protein snacking for everyone, not just hunters and gym-goers
companies.target: Whole30 / paleo / protein-conscious mainstream shoppers, increasingly GLP-1 users
companies.differentiation: Ingredient discipline plus near-bootstrapped capital efficiency — founders still control the company
companies.channels: Started DTC/Amazon; now mass retail (Costco, Target, Walmart, c-stores)
companies.vc_take: The bear case for venture in this category: ~$900M revenue built with almost no dilution. Proof the category creates real businesses — and a warning that the best operators may not need your cheque.
companies.signal: Est. ~$900M 2025 revenue (Forbes estimate); $100M credit line with Wells Fargo (Apr 2025) — estimate + verified facility

companies.name: Magic Spoon
companies.product: High-protein, zero-sugar 'childhood' cereal and treats
companies.positioning: Saturday-morning nostalgia for adults with macros
companies.target: Millennials who quit cereal for health reasons but miss it
companies.differentiation: First to make protein taste like Froot Loops; strong podcast/creator DTC engine before retail
companies.channels: DTC-led launch, now Target, Walmart, Costco, Amazon
companies.vc_take: Textbook DTC-to-retail transition and proof that 'remake a nostalgic aisle' works — but also a case study in how CAC-heavy DTC growth must convert to retail velocity to justify ~$209M raised.
companies.signal: ~$209M total funding across 5 rounds (Tracxn); $85M round in 2022 alongside Target launch — verified

companies.name: Khloud
companies.product: Protein popcorn (7g protein per serve)
companies.positioning: Celebrity-founded everyday protein snacking
companies.target: Mass Target shoppers; Kardashian audience crossover
companies.differentiation: Day-one national distribution via celebrity leverage; popcorn as an unclaimed protein format
companies.channels: Target nationwide at launch, expanding mass retail
companies.vc_take: A live experiment in whether celebrity distribution can substitute for brand-building. Watch repeat purchase, not launch velocity — that's the entire question with talent-led CPG.
companies.signal: $12M oversubscribed round (Apr 2025): Serena Ventures, WME, Shrug, K5 — verified

companies.name: Macro Mike
companies.product: Plant-based protein powders, baking mixes and peanut-butter treats
companies.positioning: Dessert-flavoured plant protein with a gut-health angle
companies.target: Australian wellness consumers; dairy-avoiders who still want brownies
companies.differentiation: Built a dessert-first plant protein brand from Burleigh Heads with zero external capital
companies.channels: DTC-led, plus AU health retail and export
companies.vc_take: The AU capital-efficiency archetype: 35+ staff, self-funded since 2016. Interesting both as a scaled bootstrapper and as a signal that AU BFY brands historically grew without venture — that's changing.
companies.signal: Self-funded; 35+ staff (Business News Australia) — company-reported

companies.name: Vitawerx
companies.product: Protein-coated chocolate, wafers and choc-coated nuts
companies.positioning: 'Healthy never tasted so good' — chocolate-first, protein hidden inside
companies.target: AU gym-adjacent consumers and health-store shoppers trading up from candy bars
companies.differentiation: Owns the protein-chocolate niche in AU health retail; broad SKU range across formats
companies.channels: AU health food stores, supplement retail, pharmacy, export to NZ
companies.vc_take: Australia's answer to the 'candy-coded protein' trend, pre-institutional-capital. Exactly the profile a US growth fund hunting a 'David of Australia' narrative would screen.
companies.signal: Founded 2015; nationally distributed in AU health retail; no disclosed external funding — company-reported

companies.name: Chief Nutrition
companies.product: Grass-fed collagen protein bars, biltong and collagen powders
companies.positioning: Real-food protein for health-span — co-founded by a nutritionist and trainers
companies.target: Paleo/whole-food Australians; CrossFit and longevity communities
companies.differentiation: Whole-food ingredient list in a category full of isolates and syrups; founder credibility in fitness media
companies.channels: DTC, Woolworths/health retail, gyms; raised via Equitise equity crowdfunding
companies.vc_take: Community-funded with a profitable ~A$4M run-rate — small, but the crowdfunding cap table is itself a brand-love signal. A seed-stage bet on the 'meat-snack-meets-collagen' wedge in AU.
companies.signal: ~A$4M annual revenue run-rate, profitable, revenue doubled YoY (Equitise raise materials) — company-reported

companies.name: FUNDAY Natural Sweets
companies.product: No-added-sugar, prebiotic-fibre gummies and chocolate
companies.positioning: Proper lollies, zero guilt — fun-first branding, not diet branding
companies.target: AU snackers and ex-candy-lovers; expanding to US
companies.differentiation: No sugar alcohols (the SmartSweets gut-complaint weakness) and 7g prebiotic fibre per serve; chemist-channel beachhead
companies.channels: Chemist Warehouse nationwide, Coles/Woolworths, Amazon AU, now US entry (fundaysweets.us)
companies.vc_take: The single most exportable AU brand on this map. Ran the SmartSweets playbook with a better formulation and a pharmacy channel insight — its US expansion is the trade I'd want to underwrite.
companies.signal: Bootstrapped at launch (founder stated no external funding plans, 2022); national Chemist Warehouse + grocery distribution; US site live — verified distribution, funding status company-reported

companies.name: SmartSweets
companies.product: Low-sugar gummies and candy
companies.positioning: 'Kick sugar, keep candy'
companies.target: Mainstream North American candy buyers cutting sugar
companies.differentiation: First mover at scale in low-sugar candy; founder-story-led brand (Tara Bosch, started at 21)
companies.channels: Mass retail across North America
companies.vc_take: The category's first big exit comp: TPG took majority control at $360M in 2020, four years from founding. Defines both the upside and the ceiling question — was that a venture outcome or a great PE outcome?
companies.signal: Majority stake sold to TPG Growth at $360M (Oct 2020) — verified

companies.name: Noshu
companies.product: Sugar-free donuts, baking mixes, frostings and chocolate ('Snackles')
companies.positioning: Real dessert experiences — donuts, not 'diet bars' — with 97–99% less sugar
companies.target: AU supermarket shoppers, diabetics, low-carb households
companies.differentiation: Proprietary sweetener systems built over a decade; owns the sugar-free bakery shelf in Coles/Woolworths
companies.channels: Coles, Woolworths, export plans (UK, EU, China)
companies.vc_take: A$4M to A$38M in four years inside mainstream grocery, now raising its first external round for international expansion — a rare AU growth-equity entry point with proven velocity data.
companies.signal: ~A$38M expected sales; first external raise underway; projecting 2.5x in 3 years (SmartCompany / company) — company-reported

companies.name: Mid-Day Squares
companies.product: Functional chocolate squares (protein + fibre, low sugar)
companies.positioning: 'Chocolate that works as hard as you' — built in public on social
companies.target: Millennial/Gen Z snackers who follow the founders' content
companies.differentiation: The founders ARE the media channel — daily behind-the-scenes content turned a chocolate bar into a show
companies.channels: Whole Foods + natural channel US/Canada, DTC
companies.vc_take: Best-in-class example of founder-as-distribution: organic content replacing paid CAC. The question is whether content-led love converts to mainstream velocity beyond the natural channel.
companies.signal: ~$16.5M raised over 3 rounds (Tracxn/Crunchbase) — verified

companies.name: Denada
companies.product: Sugar-free ice cream
companies.positioning: Indulgent ice cream, zero sugar, no asterisks on taste
companies.target: AU households cutting sugar; diabetic and keto consumers
companies.differentiation: First-mover in AU sugar-free ice cream; built distribution to 1,250+ stores in three years with no outside capital
companies.channels: AU supermarkets and independents; first export markets
companies.vc_take: Frozen is the hardest BFY logistics problem (cold chain, slotting), and Denada cracked AU shelf bootstrapped. A capital injection here is a distribution-expansion bet, not a product bet.
companies.signal: 1,250+ AU stores within 3 years, no outside investment at launch; now exporting — company-reported

companies.name: OLIPOP
companies.product: Prebiotic soda with classic flavours (Vintage Cola, Root Beer)
companies.positioning: A new kind of soda: nostalgia + digestive health, science-forward
companies.target: Mass grocery shoppers replacing legacy soda
companies.differentiation: Deepest formulation credibility in the set (microbiome research roots); profitable at scale
companies.channels: Mass retail nationwide, DTC
companies.vc_take: The standing proof that BFY beverage is venture-scale and can be PROFITABLE: $400M+ sales, first profit in 2024, $1.85B valuation. The remaining question is exit path now that Pepsi bought its rival.
companies.signal: $50M raise at $1.85B valuation (Feb 2025); $400M+ 2024 sales; profitable — verified

companies.name: Poppi
companies.product: Prebiotic soda (apple-cider-vinegar origin story)
companies.positioning: Soda's fun, social, brand-led comeback — Super Bowl ads and merch
companies.target: Gen Z and millennial ex-soda drinkers
companies.differentiation: Marketing velocity: TikTok-native brand building that outran a better-funded rival on cultural relevance
companies.channels: Mass retail, Amazon, DTC
companies.vc_take: The exit that validated the whole map: PepsiCo paid $1.95B in 2025 off ~$500M 2024 sales. Also a cautionary tale — prebiotic claims drew a class-action settlement before the deal closed.
companies.signal: Acquired by PepsiCo for $1.95B (Mar 2025); ~$500M 2024 sales — verified

companies.name: Remedy Drinks
companies.product: Live-cultured kombucha, prebiotic Sodaly, ACV switchel, shots
companies.positioning: Fermentation-led, no-sugar functional drinks from a Melbourne kitchen to 25,000 outlets
companies.target: Mainstream AU shoppers; expanding US/EU/Asia
companies.differentiation: Real fermentation at industrial scale; AU's #1 kombucha with L Catterton backing
companies.channels: 25,000+ outlets in AU plus export; unified global entity from April 2025
companies.vc_take: Australia's functional-beverage anchor asset (~A$163M revenue). Its global consolidation move reads as exit grooming — the comp every AU beverage seed deal will be priced against.
companies.signal: ~A$162.7M FY2025 revenue (IBISWorld); Series B from L Catterton & Kin Group (2023) — verified

companies.name: Naked Life
companies.product: 100% natural sugar-free sodas and non-alcoholic cocktails/spirits
companies.positioning: Premium sugar-free refreshment without artificial sweeteners
companies.target: AU mainstream grocery + the sober-curious overlap
companies.differentiation: Straddles two need-states (no sugar + no alcohol) with one brand; national grocery from a 2016 kitchen start
companies.channels: Woolworths, Coles, IGA, Dan Murphy's
companies.vc_take: Quiet national distribution across both grocery AND liquor channels is a structural advantage no US healthy-soda brand has. An obvious platform for a US prebiotic-style line extension.
companies.signal: Stocked nationally in Woolworths, Coles, IGA, Dan Murphy's; founded 2016 — company-reported

companies.name: Nexba
companies.product: Sugar-free, naturally sweetened sodas, kombucha and gut-health drinks
companies.positioning: 'Naturally sugar free' mass-market challenger
companies.target: Price-conscious AU grocery shoppers wanting healthier soft drinks
companies.differentiation: Early AU mover (Product of the Year 2017) with own natural sweetener systems
companies.channels: AU grocery (Coles partnership history), pharmacy, export attempts (UK Sainsbury's)
companies.vc_take: A lesson asset as much as an opportunity: early lead, broad portfolio, but squeezed between Remedy's fermentation credibility and private label. Shows brand focus beats SKU sprawl in beverage.
companies.signal: Founded 2010; national distribution; Product of the Year 2017 — company-reported

companies.name: Bobby
companies.product: Better-for-you cola and soft drinks (sugar-free, prebiotic)
companies.positioning: An irreverent Aussie 'new Coke' for the post-sugar generation
companies.target: Gen Z / young millennial AU convenience and grocery buyers
companies.differentiation: Brand-as-personality in a functional category; running the Poppi cultural playbook in AU
companies.channels: AU convenience, independents, grocery rollout
companies.vc_take: If the US arc (Poppi/OLIPOP) predicts AU with a 2–3 year lag, the AU window for a breakout healthy soda brand is open right now — Bobby is the most culture-forward contender in it.
companies.signal: Early-stage; expanding AU distribution — company-reported, unverified scale

companies.name: StrangeLove
companies.product: Premium craft sodas, tonics and lo-cal mixers
companies.positioning: Design-led, adult, lower-sugar refreshment — taste-first credibility
companies.target: Premium AU hospitality and grocery; cocktail/non-alc crossover
companies.differentiation: Wins on taste and design rather than functional claims — hospitality channel beachhead big brands can't fake
companies.channels: On-premise (bars/restaurants), premium grocery, DTC
companies.vc_take: The 'taste-maximalist' end of the barbell: no health claims to defend, premium price realisation, and a hospitality moat. Smaller outcome probability-weighted, but durable brand equity.
companies.signal: Established premium distribution in AU hospitality and grocery — company-reported, unverified scale

companies.name: BelliWelli
companies.product: Gut-friendly, low-FODMAP snack bars and gut-health products
companies.positioning: 'Hot girls have IBS' — destigmatising digestive health with humour
companies.target: Women with IBS/digestive issues (≈1 in 5 adults), Gen Z wellness
companies.differentiation: Community-first growth: viral billboards and TikTok built the brand before retail did
companies.channels: DTC, Amazon, expanding US retail (Target, Sprouts)
companies.vc_take: The cleanest example of an underserved-condition wedge becoming a lifestyle brand. $10M Series B off viral organic growth — the CAC profile every DTC food brand claims and few have.
companies.signal: $10M Series B (Oct 2024); ~$26M total raised — verified

companies.name: Fodbods
companies.product: Low-FODMAP, gut-friendly snack bars and protein bars
companies.positioning: Science-certified safe snacking for sensitive stomachs (Monash FODMAP heritage country)
companies.target: Australians with IBS and food intolerances
companies.differentiation: Australia invented the low-FODMAP framework (Monash University) — local credibility moat; angel-backed by Scale Investors
companies.channels: DTC, AU pharmacy and health retail, Coles
companies.vc_take: BelliWelli's thesis with an unfair Australian advantage: Monash is the global FODMAP authority. A small cheque with a clear US-expansion narrative riding clinical credibility.
companies.signal: Seed funding from Scale Investors (AU angel network) — verified investor, undisclosed amount

companies.name: Sweet Loren's
companies.product: Allergen-free, gluten-free refrigerated cookie dough and pastry
companies.positioning: 'Everyone deserves a delicious cookie' — top-14-allergen-free indulgence
companies.target: Allergy households (an entire family switches when one member must), celiac consumers
companies.differentiation: Owns the refrigerated dough niche incumbents ignored; founder survivor story drives authentic brand trust
companies.channels: 30,000+ US grocery doors incl. mainstream chains (company-reported)
companies.vc_take: Allergen-free is bought by the household, not the individual — basket-level loyalty with near-zero churn. Quietly one of the best repeat-purchase profiles in the whole map.
companies.signal: National US grocery distribution; largely founder-controlled — company-reported

companies.name: Goodles
companies.product: Protein- and veggie-boosted boxed mac & cheese and noodles
companies.positioning: 'Noodles, gooder' — upgrading the most nostalgic box in the pantry
companies.target: Millennial parents and comfort-food eaters who read labels
companies.differentiation: 14g protein + hidden veg in a true Kraft-blue-box taste experience; celebrity co-founder (Gal Gadot) used sparingly
companies.channels: Target, Walmart, Whole Foods, Amazon
companies.vc_take: L Catterton-backed shot at a $9B sleepy aisle. Mac & cheese has guaranteed household penetration — the bet is purely on conversion and velocity, not behaviour change. That's the right kind of CPG bet.
companies.signal: $19.4M raised ($13M Series A, Sep 2023, L Catterton) — verified

companies.name: immi
companies.product: High-protein, low-carb instant ramen
companies.positioning: The ramen you loved at uni, re-engineered for adult macros
companies.target: Asian-American and mainstream millennial comfort-food eaters; keto/low-carb
companies.differentiation: First credible BFY entry in a 100B-serving global category; founders are ex-tech operators (Kevin Lee, Kevin Chanthasiriphan) with cultural authenticity
companies.channels: DTC-first, Amazon, Whole Foods, Target
companies.vc_take: Ramen is one of the most habitual, highest-frequency foods on earth with zero healthy incumbent. If immi nails taste parity, the repeat-purchase math beats almost any snack on this map.
companies.signal: ~$29M raised over 4 rounds; latest round Dec 2024 (Tracxn) — verified

companies.name: Mingle
companies.product: Natural, low-sugar seasonings, sauces and gravies
companies.positioning: 'No nasties' flavour staples — clean-label everyday cooking, not dieting
companies.target: AU home cooks and parents replacing legacy sauce brands
companies.differentiation: Took on AU's most concentrated grocery duopoly shelf (sauces/seasonings) and won national ranging in both majors
companies.channels: Woolworths and Coles nationally, DTC
companies.vc_take: Pantry staples are the stickiest repeat purchase in food. Mingle proved an indie can displace incumbent sauce brands in the world's most consolidated grocery market — rare velocity evidence.
companies.signal: National Woolworths + Coles ranging; early accelerator funding only (PitchBook/Crunchbase) — verified distribution

companies.name: Siete Foods
companies.product: Grain-free tortillas, chips, salsas and Mexican-American heritage foods
companies.positioning: Family-story-led, grain-free comfort food ('Juntos es Mejor')
companies.target: Health-conscious households + Mexican-American heritage consumers
companies.differentiation: Authentic family founding story (7 Garza family members) + allergen-conscious formulation in a giant everyday category
companies.channels: National US grocery and mass
companies.vc_take: The exit comp for clean-label comfort: PepsiCo paid $1.2B in 2024. Proof that heritage + health + family story is an acquirable combination at scale.
companies.signal: Acquired by PepsiCo for $1.2B (announced 2024) — verified

companies.name: LesserEvil
companies.product: Organic popcorn, puffs and 'Space Balls' snacks (coconut-oil popped)
companies.positioning: Mindful, organic snacking with playful cosmic branding
companies.target: Natural-channel families trading up from conventional salty snacks
companies.differentiation: Owns its manufacturing (rare for indie CPG) — margin and innovation-speed advantage that made it acquirable
companies.channels: National US natural + mass retail
companies.vc_take: The 2025 exit that priced clean-label salty snacks: Hershey paid ~$750M (WSJ). Note WHY it won: self-manufacturing. Supply-chain ownership is the recurring moat across this map's biggest outcomes.
companies.signal: Acquired by Hershey, ~$750M reported (closed Nov 2025) — verified deal, price per WSJ report

companies.name: Feastables
companies.product: Chocolate bars with simplified ingredient lists
companies.positioning: MrBeast's chocolate — creator audience converted to shelf velocity
companies.target: Gen Z / Gen Alpha; gifting and impulse purchase
companies.differentiation: 200M+ subscriber distribution engine; 'cleaner than Hershey's' ingredient framing without health-brand pricing
companies.channels: Walmart-led mass retail (deliberately not DTC)
companies.vc_take: $0 to $250M revenue in under 3 years, profitably, by skipping DTC entirely and putting creator media behind Walmart shelf. The most important distribution lesson on this map — and the most key-person-dependent asset on it.
companies.signal: ~$250M 2024 revenue, ~$20M profit; ~$520M projected 2025 (reported) — credible third-party reporting, not audited

companies.name: Twisted Healthy Treats
companies.product: Lower-sugar, hidden-veg kids' frozen treats and ice creams
companies.positioning: Treats parents say yes to — kid-tested taste, school-canteen compliant
companies.target: AU parents; school canteens (traffic-light food policies)
companies.differentiation: Canteen-compliance as a regulatory moat: AU school food policies effectively mandate products like this
companies.channels: AU grocery, school canteens, food service
companies.vc_take: Kids' BFY is bought on rules, not willpower — school policy is a built-in B2B2C channel US brands don't have. Small today, but the structural demand is legislated.
companies.signal: AU grocery + canteen distribution — company-reported, unverified scale

companies.name: Blue Dinosaur
companies.product: Paleo-style real-food bars and kids' lunchbox snacks
companies.positioning: Sunshine-coast real-food energy — minimal ingredients, lunchbox-safe lines
companies.target: Active AU families; surf/outdoor lifestyle consumers
companies.differentiation: Lifestyle-brand identity (surf culture) in a category of clinical macro brands; school-safe SKUs
companies.channels: Woolworths, Coles, AU convenience, export
companies.vc_take: Demonstrates the AU pattern: lifestyle authenticity over functional claims. A consolidation candidate — the AU bar shelf has too many subscale brands and someone will roll it up.
companies.signal: National AU grocery distribution — company-reported, unverified scale
